partner_context.their_ambition: You regulate one of the world's great public ferry networks — the cross-harbour Star Ferry, the six major outlying-island lifelines, and dozens of in-harbour services — and you've committed to electrifying it under the Climate Action Plan 2050.
partner_context.their_pressure: An ageing diesel fleet, fare and viability pressure on island routes, and a carbon-neutrality target before 2050 all demand a cleaner, more efficient fleet.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to the ferries you already run — faster and far more efficient per passenger-mile, improving both the climate outcome and the economics of keeping island services viable, alongside the heritage Star Ferry.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Hong Kong SAR · Transport Department
hero.title: A zero-emission ferry network for Hong Kong
hero.subtitle: A faster, quieter, far more efficient tier on the cross-harbour and outlying-island routes — directly serving the Climate Action Plan 2050 and the viability of island services.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a zero-emission foiling tier to Hong Kong's ferry network — across Victoria Harbour and out to the islands. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent and roughly an order of magnitude more efficient per passenger-mile, improving both Climate Action Plan 2050 outcomes and the economics that keep lifeline island services running.

why_now: Hong Kong runs ~95 ferry routes and has already chosen electric and hybrid ferries as the decarbonization path for an ageing diesel fleet, with a government pilot scheme underway and a carbon-neutrality target before 2050. Island routes also face fare and viability pressure. A far more efficient zero-emission vessel serves both the climate target and island-service economics. A demo vessel is proving the model at scale in the Maldives.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into Hong Kong's public transport as a faster, cleaner ferry tier — integrated with the MTR and bus network and feeding the island communities.

proof_points.claim: Hong Kong runs one of the world's great ferry networks.
proof_points.evidence: ~95 licensed ferry routes (11 within Victoria Harbour, 84 serving other areas), including the six major outlying-island lifelines and the Star Ferry.

proof_points.claim: Electrification is already the chosen path.
proof_points.evidence: A government pilot scheme is testing electric in-harbour and hybrid outlying-island ferries, under the Climate Action Plan 2050 carbon-neutrality target.

proof_points.claim: Island-service viability is a live public concern.
proof_points.evidence: Outlying-island routes face fare and licence-renewal pressure; a far more efficient vessel improves the economics that keep them running.

proof_points.claim: The network model is proven and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing proving the model in the Maldives.

objections.concern: Can a foiling vessel operate in Victoria Harbour's traffic?
objections.response: Yes — foiling is software-governed, with geofenced no-foil zones and speed limits across the cross-harbour fairways and ferry lanes; it flies only where cleared and runs conventionally everywhere else.

objections.concern: Will it sit alongside the Star Ferry?
objections.response: Yes — the foiling tier is additive, an express option alongside the heritage Star Ferry, not a replacement for it.

objections.concern: How does this help island-service viability?
objections.response: Foiling hulls use roughly an order of magnitude less energy per passenger-mile than the diesel fleet, directly improving the unit economics that keep lifeline island routes running.

close.title: A zero-emission upgrade for the ferries Hong Kong loves.
close.body: Start cross-harbour and on Lamma, scale across the island lifelines and in-harbour routes — a faster, cleaner ferry tier that serves the Climate Action Plan 2050 and keeps island services viable, alongside the heritage Star Ferry.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the piers and ferry terminals already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel ferry fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the range excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

levers: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a ferry network Hong Kong already runs at scale and is committed to electrifying. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent, low-wake and roughly an order of magnitude more efficient per passenger-mile than the diesel fleet — improving both island-service economics and Climate Action Plan 2050 outcomes, while sitting alongside the heritage Star Ferry.

Hong Kong has already chosen electric/hybrid ferries as the decarbonization path for an ageing diesel fleet, and is grappling with the cost of keeping island services viable. Zero-emission foiling vessels are faster, far more efficient per passenger-mile, and quieter — directly serving the Climate Action Plan 2050 target while improving island-service economics.
